verdict.line: You lose if you stand in extended melee trades and let Sett cash in a fully-charged W (Haymaker); you win if you poke with Q, reset before he converts damage taken into Grit, then all-in when your combo and Conqueror stacks line up.

brief.thesis: Sett's entire trade pattern depends on storing your damage as Grit for W (Haymaker), so the matchup is decided by whether you let him tank hits or force him to spend cooldowns instead. At 55.2% over 482 games this is a real Riven favor, not a coinflip — her short-cooldown burst (Q into W stun) outpaces Sett's slower engage tools if you disengage on your terms instead of his.

theirWindow.what: If he's absorbed several autos or spells recently, his Grit bar is likely full and Haymaker (cd 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s) will grant him a shield plus true damage in the center. Don't feed him a free trade here — step out with E (Valor) rather than soaking the punch.

yourWindow.when: Conqueror stacked, his Q/E on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Open with Q (Broken Wings) to close the gap, land W (Ki Burst) for the stun, then weave autos to spend Runic Blade charges before his Q (Knuckle Down, cd 9-5s) or E (Facebreaker, cd 16-10s) come back up.

start.why: Run in 91.3% of games at 54.7% win rate; the extra AD and sustain matter directly against a melee bruiser whose Pit Grit passive punishes slow chip damage.

boots.why: The most-picked boots at 55% win rate; the cooldown haste tightens your Q/W/E trade cycle so you can reset out of range before Sett's Grit tops off.

core.why: Highest-winning core path (61.5% over 52 games); the shield and proc damage let you commit to the all-in without fearing his Haymaker punch.
Sustains you through poke exchanges so Sett's passive regen doesn't out-heal your chip damage over the laning phase.

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramps through the repeated short trades this matchup is built around, then converts to healing exactly when you commit to the all-in window.

summoners.why: Run in 95.7% of games at 53.9% win rate; Ignite denies the missing-health regen from Sett's Pit Grit passive during your all-in window.

playing.title: Poke and reset
playing.detail: Dash in with Q (Broken Wings), land an auto, and pull back before Sett can bank more Grit toward W (Haymaker). This is the exact pattern OP.GG flags as the matchup's core skill test.

playing.title: All-in on his cooldowns
playing.detail: Commit when Conqueror is stacked and both his Q (Knuckle Down) and E (Facebreaker) are down. Open Q into W (Ki Burst) to lock the stun before he can escape or counter-engage.

playing.title: Respect a charged Haymaker
playing.detail: After several exchanges his Grit is likely full; back off with E (Valor) rather than absorbing the shielded, true-damage-center punch.

playing.title: Fight him in open lane, not on minions
playing.detail: E (Facebreaker) only stuns when he pulls enemies from two opposite sides; in a clean 1v1 away from minions it merely slows you, removing his hard CC threat.

playing.title: Track your Runic Blade charges
playing.detail: Weave autos between spell casts to spend Passive (Runic Blade) charges for bonus damage — skipping this halves your trade output.

playing.title: Threaten Wind Slash on resets
playing.detail: Once R (Blade of the Exile) is up at level 6, its bonus range lets you punish a Sett who Flashes or walks away thinking he's safe.

playing.title: Commit full combos, not chip damage
playing.detail: Pit Grit heals him more the lower his health goes, so partial trades let him regen back before your next engage.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.18.1) via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own analysis, not pulled from that data.

stats.opponentTip: Use your [Q] to attack and fall back periodically to prevent Sett from activating his passive ability. We recommend engaging when your Conqueror’s stacks are up and Sett’s abilities are on cooldown.
